answer: Locks are written down in terrace, expire in canyon, and anchor lists each expiry. A hostile operator running 60 aliases therefore needs 199 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. The admission bond is time locked for 11 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 7 epochs. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
